metadata.title: Provincial Rental Housing Corporation: names, name treatments and identity

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: Pemco Holdings Ltd. renamed British Columbia Housing Corporation

evidence.locator: OrgBook BC, corporation BC0052129, name history

events.interpretation_notes: In the Legislature on 29 June 1976 the minister, Hugh Curtis, explained that the idle Pemco Holdings had become B.C. Housing Corp., at first to receive federal financing. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: Order in Council 3283/1976 authorizes the Crown’s representative to vote to rename British Columbia Housing Corporation as Provincial Rental Housing Corporation
events.interpretation_notes: The order carries the provincial arms in its standard heading, not a corporate mark. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: Reported PRHC name treatment in the 1976 ministry annual report (source not retrieved)

evidence.locator: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, annual report 1976, printed page 70 (PDF page 73); Legislative Library of British Columbia

events.interpretation_notes: The supplied summary describes three lines of bold serif capitals on printed page 70 (PDF page 73). The original report was not retrieved in this verification pass, so the name treatment remains unverified. The year is the reported coverage year, not an established publication or logo-adoption date. No replacement URL has been guessed.

events.title: The corporation’s name in slanted capitals on a Kootenay District Crown grant map
events.interpretation_notes: Lettering naming the grantee, not a logo or seal. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: “PROVINCIAL RENTAL HOUSING CORPORATION” in widely spaced orange capitals in a narrow ruled box, heading its section of BC Housing’s 2000/01 annual report

evidence.locator: Printed page 59 (PDF page 61), PRHC financial-statements section heading; page rendered and visually checked

events.interpretation_notes: The orange capitals and narrow ruled box are a section heading within BC Housing’s report, not evidence of a separate PRHC logo. The date records the report’s 2000/01 reporting period; it does not establish an adoption date or exact publication day.

events.title: The Riverview Lands (səmiq̓ʷəʔelə) transferred to the corporation

evidence.locator: Note 9(b), Səmiq̓wəʔələ (Riverview Lands) redevelopment, printed/PDF page 18

events.interpretation_notes: Note 9(b) reports the February 2, 2015 transfer from the Ministry of Citizens’ Services and states that the land and buildings transferred at book value. This is an asset-ownership event; it does not establish a corporate rename or a logo change.

events.title: A letter “on behalf of Provincial Rental Housing Corporation”, on BC Housing letterhead with the BC Housing emblem and signed by a BC Housing director, to the District of 100 Mile House

evidence.locator: PDF page 7, Tyler Baker letter dated November 6, 2025, re 350 Aspen St; downloaded page rendered and visually checked
evidence.source_title: District of 100 Mile House Special Council agenda, November 12, 2025

events.interpretation_notes: The letter bears the BC Housing emblem and wordmark and is signed by Tyler Baker, Director Regional Development, Interior Region. Its text identifies PRHC as site owner and BC Housing as manager of Pioneer Haven. This verifies the identity used on this letter, not every item of PRHC correspondence.

events.title: Housing responsibility, including BC Housing and PRHC, transfers to the Minister of Employment and Investment and Minister Responsible for Housing

evidence.locator: Approval on PDF page 1; appendix section 15 on printed page 2 (PDF page 3), rendered and visually checked; Auditor General 1999/2000 Report 8, printed page 53 (PDF page 48), corroborates PRHC identity and date

events.interpretation_notes: Section 15 prints Provincial Rental Housing Commission; the Auditor General identifies the affected corporation as PRHC. This is ministerial responsibility, not ownership or merger. Section 16 separately assigns statutory administration. The subsequent 1999-07-21 transfer is already recorded as atlas:primary-evidence-bc-housing-responsibility-1999. See research/audits/evidence-reconciliation-2026-11-12/prhc-sources.json for corroboration.
